subject: Clarify incident notification & cross-border evidence cooperation
messages:
From: Priya Shah <priya.shah@luminahealth.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: LuminaHealth Legal <legal@luminahealth.com>
Date: Sun, 20 Dec 2026 17:12:00 +0000
Subject: Data incident notification wording & cross-border evidence transfer

Hi Markus / Kim,

Thanks for taking this quickly. We're updating our incident response playbook and need to confirm how Redwood's DPA language maps to a couple of scenarios we commonly see in EU health customers. Two quick asks:

1) Notification window: our contract teams expect a firm 72-hour initial notification for incidents that may affect LuminaHealth data (P1/P2). Can you confirm Redwood's commitment window and whether that includes time to triage internally before customer notification?

2) Evidence transfer & cross-border: sometimes forensic artifacts need to be exported for our EU-based forensics partner (Forensica). We need to understand (a) whether Redwood will export full telemetry and disk snapshots if requested under a DPA; (b) whether you require an export-control or Law Enforcement overlay that would delay transfer; and (c) any subprocessors involved in handling exported data.

Attached are a suggested list of artifacts and formats (Lumina_Requested_Format_Specs.pdf) to make this concrete. Legal is cc'd — if you prefer, we can run a short MOP (mutual action plan) for the handoff.

Appreciate clarity on scope and any contractual constraints.

Best,
Priya
Security & Privacy Lead | LuminaHealth
Attachments: Lumina_Requested_Format_Specs.pdf

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Priya Shah <priya.shah@luminahealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 20 Dec 2026 18:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Data incident notification wording & cross-border evidence transfer

Priya —

Thanks, and this is a good, pragmatic set of asks. High level answers first, then suggestions for contract language and operational steps below.

1) Notification window: We currently commit to "initial customer notification within 72 hours of confirming a security incident that affects Customer Data." To be explicit: that 72-hour window begins when we have confirmed that Customer Data was impacted (not from first detection). We understand customers sometimes want notification tied to detection; we're willing to discuss language that clarifies both detection and confirmation milestones.

2) Evidence transfer & cross-border:
  - Export scope: Redwood can provide telemetry, request logs, and VM snapshots where applicable. For disk-level artifacts, there are operational constraints (depending on Dedicated vs Hosted deployments) — we can export forensics-friendly artifacts for both Dedicated and hosted customers, but for hosted accounts we require a scoped forensic request and legal approval.
  - Law enforcement/export controls: Redwood maintains a process to evaluate lawful requests; in day-to-day DPA cooperation we do not add a separate export-control review that would extend the notification SLA, but any third-party legal holds or foreign government orders may require clarification and could affect timelines.
  - Subprocessors: Our primary storage and telemetry subprocessors are listed in the DPA appendix; when we export artifacts to a customer-designated EU forensics partner, Redwood performs a one-time transfer and does not retain copies beyond agreed retention in the transfer scope unless otherwise requested.

Operational suggestion: let's draft a short appendix to the DPA — "Forensic Evidence Handoff" — that: (a) lists artifact types and formats (we'll align to your PDF); (b) sets the handoff SLA (we propose 5 business days from confirmed incident to deliver scoped artifacts for hosted customers, 3 business days for Dedicated customers); and (c) requires a signed FoU (forensic operations) form from the receiving party and a signed DPA amendment.

I'm looping Ben (ops) and Kim (legal) to weigh in on feasibility and language. If agreeable, we can turn this into a 30-minute sync and Redwood will produce a draft appendix by EOD Wed.

— Markus
Markus Klein | VP, Legal & Compliance | Redwood Inference

From: Samir Khan <samir.khan@forensica.io>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@luminahealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Dec 2026 08:25:00 +00:00
Subject: Re: Data incident notification wording & cross-border evidence transfer

Hi all — quick operational note from the forensics side.

We can accept the artifact list in Lumina_Requested_Format_Specs.pdf. A couple of clarifications that affect turnaround:

- For hosted telemetry exports we typically request an anonymized token map alongside logs so we can correlate sessions without requiring full PII flows. Is Redwood able to provide a mapping key under a separate encrypted channel?
- Transfer mechanism: preferred is scp over dedicated SFTP or an encrypted drive courier for very large VM snapshots. Please confirm maximum single-file sizes we should expect.

We can sign a standard FoU and storage isolation addendum. If Redwood can commit to the 5-business-day window for hosted accounts (and 3 for Dedicated) that aligns with our operational tempo.

Thanks,
Samir
CTO, Forensica (third-party forensics)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Priya Shah <priya.shah@luminahealth.com>, Samir Khan <samir.khan@forensica.io>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Dec 2026 12:40:00 +00:00
Subject: Re: Data incident notification wording & cross-border evidence transfer

Priya / Samir —

Appreciate the practical list. A few concrete follow-ups from legal/ops so we can put this in an appendix:

- We'll draft the "Forensic Evidence Handoff" appendix with the proposed SLAs (5 bd hosted / 3 bd Dedicated). If Lumina prefers a shorter initial notification tied to detection rather than confirmation, propose this language: "Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to notify Customer within 48 hours of detection and will provide a confirmed incident notification within 72 hours of confirmation." That preserves our internal triage window while giving customers earlier visibility.
- On the mapping key: Redwood can provide an encrypted, time-limited mapping file for correlation. We'll include requirements for secure channel delivery in the appendix.
- Transfer mechanics: we'll support SFTP (strongly preferred) and scp. Single-file size: up to 200GB; for larger images we recommend chunked transfer or shipment of encrypted drives (courier). We'll include an operational checklist covering checksums and chain-of-custody notes.

Action items:
  * Redwood (Kim) to circulate draft appendix + FoU template by Wed 23 Dec EOD GMT.
  * Lumina (Priya) to confirm acceptance of the 5/3 bd SLA and the 48/72 detection/confirmation language, or propose edits.
  * Forensica (Samir) to review transfer mechanics and confirm chunking strategy if needed.

If those align, Ben will coordinate a short SOW for the export work if needed.

Thanks — happy holidays and we'll aim to get the draft over this week.

Kimberly Park
Sr. Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
Attachments referenced: DPA_Evidence_Transfer_Appendix_v1.docx
